factual_methodology.summary: UN WPP 2024 estimates and projections, WUP 2025 city classification, IBGE 2024 population trajectory, SOFI 2026, UNICEF/WHO mortality 2024, UNFPA 2025 survey, OECD 2025 pension outlook, FAO SOLAW 2025 and IPCC emissions distribution are correctly dated and distinguish stocks, flows, rates and scenarios.

source_integrity.summary: Both editions cite 21 retrievable named source URLs spanning 13 unique hosts; direct UN/UNFPA/WHO/UNICEF/FAO/OECD/World Bank/IBGE/IPCC and IOM sources are matched to defined claims.

source_vintage_and_cutoff.summary: Demographic baseline WPP 2024 not portrayed as a measured 2026 headcount. WHO 2026, SOFI 2026 and IOM 2026 updates distinguished from observations referring to 2024/2025. Future 2054/2080/2100 quantities identified as projections.

editorial_publication_readiness.summary: Original long-form bilingual study organized in 17 progressive sections, without self-referential report scaffolding. Distinguishes population quantities from per capita outcomes and safeguards reproductive autonomy.

visual_evidence_readiness.summary: Each edition contains four explicit quantitative charts, four structured Markdown tables, one mapped regional comparison, one causal flow and one mindmap. Identical numerical chart arrays and matched meaning across languages. Historical and projected values differentiated in surrounding prose.

research_depth.summary: Deep coherent treatment of prehistory, mortality, fertility, momentum, global and national transitions, psychological choice, economic dependency, welfare financing, migration, urbanization, food, water, climate, rights and three falsifiable futures.

evidence_traceability.summary: Quantities trace to referenced tables and institutionally dated releases: 3.31/2.25 TFR; 2.5/6.2/8.2 world population; 10.3/10.2 projected; child mortality; 63/48/126 country groups and -14/+5.3/+38 project group changes; 645 million hungry; 304 million migrants; 220.425 million Brazil peak.

counterfactual_review.summary: Three conditional futures provide variables and observations that would weaken preferred mechanisms; technology, fertility, food production and fiscal outcomes are not presented as mechanical consequences of headcount.

translation_equivalence.summary: Both editions have 17 sections and 21 source references with matching numerical claims, visual types, scenario qualifications, age definitions and rights commitments.

social_change_evidence.summary: Ageing, migration, fertility choices and employment relate to observed or projected age structure and public finance, without demographic determinism.

contrary_evidence: Population declines can coexist with productivity and income gains, weakening a simple GDP-headcount association.
Greater farming productivity does not automatically remove hunger if financial access and logistics remain unequal.
Smaller fertility rates do not immediately reduce headcount due to past large cohorts and longer lives.
Higher population density can improve infrastructure efficiency when institutions deliver services.
Resource impacts vary greatly with consumption and emissions intensity, not just population.
limitations: WPP 2024 remains the latest verified UN population projection revision at the editorial cutoff; future revisions may materially change the peak.
Pre-1950 world population is a reconstruction using changing source methods, not a direct census.
UNFPA/YouGov multicountry findings should not be generalized as representative of every country.
OECD working-age projections, IBGE national projections and UN global projections differ in horizon and population.
On-platform structural and evidentiary checks passed; complete npm validation is deferred to the GitHub Actions build as no local repository execution is available through the connector.
notes: QA-gated review of current HEAD and SHA-bound v2 research files. Includes accessible primary-source spot checks and complete bilingual visual/numeric parity tests; does not create or modify public reports. Not a substitute for independent human peer review.

producer_checks.research_depth: EN ~5481 substantive words, PT-BR ~5798 substantive words; 17 sections each; 21 source URLs each across 13 hosts
producer_checks.evidence_vintage: UN WPP 2024 WUP 2025 WHO UNICEF 2026 SOFI 2026 OECD 2025 IBGE 2024; observations vs future projections explicitly separated
producer_checks.visual_evidence: 4 matched numerical charts plus 4 evidence tables, 1 flow, 1 map and 1 mindmap in both languages
producer_checks.novelty: Integrates long-run demographic regime change, population momentum, choice constraints, uneven global stages, sectoral resource pressure, class emissions and national economic capacity.
producer_checks.counterfactuals: Labour absorption, reproductive autonomy, adaptation productivity, environmental and infrastructure trajectories specify conditions that weaken each scenario.
producer_checks.research_ethics: Avoids coercive pronatalism/antinatalism, distinguishes rights and outcomes, and does not turn model scenarios into certainties.

limitations: WPP 2024 remains the latest verified official UN demographic baseline at cutoff; projections are conditional and revised periodically.
Historic population reconstruction before 1950 combines sources with substantial uncertainty.
Urbanization 2025 degree-of-urbanization definition differs from older national definitions.
Multi-country UNFPA fertility-intentions survey is not a census of worldwide preferences.
UN population scenarios, IBGE country projections, SOFI 2026 hunger and OECD pensions use distinct populations, dates and measures.
